subject: Chemistry
name: Theory (Core)
description: Core theory covering the Periodic Table, halogens, water and ions, sulfur and compounds, metals, rate of reaction, organic chemistry, and nitrogen compounds.

parts.label: a
parts.question: Fig. 1.1 shows part of the Periodic Table containing: H, He, C, N, O, Mg, Na, Al, Cl, K, Ca, Fe, Cu, Br, I. Each symbol may be used once, more than once or not at all. Give the symbol of the element that forms 78% by volume of clean, dry air.

parts.label: b
parts.question: Give the symbol of the element that has an atom with a complete outer electron shell.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Give the symbol of the element that has an atom with five occupied electron shells.

parts.label: d
parts.question: Give the symbol of the element that forms an ion with a charge of 2–.

parts.label: e
parts.question: Give the symbol of the element that forms an ion that gives a green precipitate on addition of aqueous sodium hydroxide.

parts.label: f
parts.question: Give the symbol of the element that is used in food containers because of its resistance to corrosion.

parts.label: a(i)
parts.question: Table 2.1 shows properties of halogens: fluorine (mp –220°C, bp –188°C, density 0.0016 g/cm³), chlorine (mp –101°C, bp –35°C, density 0.0032 g/cm³), bromine (density 3.1 g/cm³), iodine (mp +114°C, bp +184°C). Predict the melting point of bromine.

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.question: Predict the density of iodine at room temperature and pressure.

parts.label: a(iii)
parts.question: Predict the physical state of chlorine at –10°C. Give a reason for your answer.

parts.label: b(i)
parts.question: The equation for the reaction of aqueous chlorine with aqueous potassium iodide is: Cl₂ + 2KI → I₂ + 2KCl. Choose the word which best describes this type of chemical reaction. Circle your answer.

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.question: Explain why aqueous iodine does not react with aqueous potassium chloride.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Complete the diagram to show the electronic configuration of a chlorine atom (atomic number 17). Draw the electron shells: 2,8,7.

parts.label: d
parts.question: Describe a test for chlorine.

parts.label: a
parts.question: Water from natural sources contains dissolved gases. Choose from the list the gas that is essential for aquatic life. Circle your answer.

parts.label: b(i)
parts.question: Polluted water may contain harmful substances such as metal compounds, plastics, nitrates and phosphates. Name one other harmful substance which is present in polluted water.

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.question: State why nitrates are harmful to aquatic life.

parts.label: c(i)
parts.question: Table 3.1 shows masses of ions in mg per 1000 cm³ of polluted water: NH₄⁺ (0.5), Ca²⁺ (2.2), Cl⁻ (2.5), HCO₃⁻ (12.0), Mg²⁺ (0.8), NO₃⁻ (0.4), K⁺ (8.3), SiO₃²⁻ (8.0), Na⁺ (10.2), SO₄²⁻ (0.2), Sn²⁺ (0.4). Name the negative ion present in the highest concentration.

parts.label: c(ii)
parts.question: State the name of the NH₄⁺ ion.

parts.label: c(iii)
parts.question: Calculate the mass of calcium ions present in 200 cm³ of polluted water.

parts.label: d(i)
parts.question: CuSO₄(s) + 5H₂O(l) ⇋ CuSO₄•5H₂O(s). State the meaning of the term hydrated.

parts.label: d(ii)
parts.question: Describe how hydrated copper(II) sulfate is changed to anhydrous copper(II) sulfate.

parts.label: e
parts.question: Complete the symbol equation for the reaction of sodium with water. 2Na + .....H₂O → 2NaOH + ............

parts.label: a
parts.question: Sulfur has several isotopes. Define the term isotopes.

parts.label: b
parts.question: Deduce the number of protons, neutrons and electrons in the sulfide ion ³⁶S²⁻ (atomic number 16).

parts.label: c(i)
parts.question: Fig. 4.1 shows an incomplete reaction pathway diagram (energy vs progress of reaction) for sulfur burning in oxygen to produce sulfur dioxide. Complete the diagram by writing S + O₂ on the left (higher energy, reactants) and SO₂ on the right (lower energy, products).

parts.label: c(ii)
parts.question: Explain how the reaction pathway diagram shows that the reaction is exothermic.

parts.label: c(iii)
parts.question: Complete this sentence using a word from the list: products, reactants, sulfur, surroundings. An exothermic reaction transfers thermal energy to the ............................. .

parts.label: d(i)
parts.question: Fig. 4.2 shows the apparatus for electrolysis of dilute sulfuric acid using graphite electrodes (power supply, two electrodes in a beaker). Label the diagram to show the cathode and the electrolyte.

parts.label: d(ii)
parts.question: Name the products and state the observations at the positive and negative electrodes during electrolysis of dilute sulfuric acid with graphite electrodes.

parts.label: e
parts.question: Complete the word equation for the reaction of dilute sulfuric acid with sodium carbonate. sulfuric acid + sodium carbonate → ........................ + ........................ + ........................

parts.label: f
parts.question: A few drops of thymolphthalein indicator are added to dilute sulfuric acid. State the colour of the solution.

parts.label: a
parts.question: Iron is a transition element. Potassium is an element in Group I of the Periodic Table. State two differences in the physical properties of iron compared to potassium.

parts.label: b
parts.question: Carbon is used to extract iron from iron ore in a blast furnace. State two uses of carbon in the extraction process.

parts.label: c(i)
parts.question: Steel is an alloy of iron. State the meaning of the term alloy.

parts.label: c(ii)
parts.question: State why alloys are more useful than pure metals.

parts.label: d
parts.question: Table 5.1 shows observations of four metals with dilute hydrochloric acid: iron (bubbles form slowly), lead (no bubbles formed), magnesium (bubbles form rapidly), nickel (bubbles form very slowly). Put the four metals in order of reactivity, least reactive first.

parts.label: a(i)
parts.question: A student investigates the reaction of zinc with three concentrations of dilute hydrochloric acid (1.0, 1.5, 2.0 mol/dm³). Table 6.1 shows times: 200s, 100s, 150s. Complete the table by matching the concentrations to the times. (Higher concentration = faster = shorter time.)

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.question: Describe the effect on the time taken for the zinc to finish reacting with 2.0 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid with no catalyst present. All other conditions stay the same.

parts.label: a(iii)
parts.question: Describe the effect on the time taken when the surface area of the zinc is increased. All other conditions stay the same.

parts.label: b
parts.question: Crystals of zinc chloride can be prepared by reacting excess zinc with dilute hydrochloric acid. Choose from the list the method used to separate the unreacted zinc from the reaction mixture. Circle your answer.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Zinc chloride is soluble in water. Choose one other compound that is soluble in water. Tick one box.

parts.label: a(i)
parts.question: Fig. 7.1 shows the displayed formula of mesaconic acid (a molecule with a C=C double bond and two COOH carboxylic acid groups). On the diagram, draw a circle around one carboxylic acid functional group.

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.question: Deduce the molecular formula of mesaconic acid (structure shows 5 carbons, 6 hydrogens, 4 oxygens).

parts.label: a(iii)
parts.question: Mesaconic acid is a colourless compound. Describe the colour change when excess mesaconic acid is added to aqueous bromine.

parts.label: b
parts.question: Ethanoic acid belongs to the homologous series of carboxylic acids. Define the term homologous series.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Complete the word equation for the reaction of ethanoic acid with magnesium. ethanoic acid + magnesium → ........................ + ........................

parts.label: d
parts.question: Ethanoic acid reacts with ethanol to produce an organic product with molecular formula C₄H₈O₂. Complete Table 7.1 to calculate the relative molecular mass. C: 4×12=48, H: 8×1=8, O: 2×16=32. Find Mr.

parts.label: e
parts.question: Ethanol can be manufactured by fermentation. Complete the word equation for one other method of manufacturing ethanol. ................................ + ................................ → ethanol

parts.label: a
parts.question: Nitrogen is a non-metal. Nitrogen is a poor electrical conductor. Describe two other physical properties which are typical of non-metals.

parts.label: b(i)
parts.question: Oxides of nitrogen are air pollutants which contribute to acid rain. State one source of oxides of nitrogen in the air.

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.question: State one other adverse effect of oxides of nitrogen.

parts.label: c(i)
parts.question: Ammonia is a simple molecule with covalent bonds. Describe a covalent bond.

parts.label: c(ii)
parts.question: Complete Fig. 8.1 to show the dot-and-cross diagram for a molecule of ammonia (NH₃). Show outer shell electrons only. N has 5 outer electrons, each H has 1; three N-H covalent bonds and one lone pair on N.

parts.label: c(iii)
parts.question: Aqueous ammonia is alkaline. Choose from the list the pH value that is alkaline. Circle your answer.

parts.label: c(iv)
parts.question: A long glass tube is set up with cotton wool soaked in aqueous ammonia at one end and damp red litmus paper at the other. At first the litmus paper does not turn blue. After a short time the litmus paper turns blue. Explain these results in terms of the kinetic particle theory.
